perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- Ethan is a plumber and long-time friend of Gary Guo, a doctor. They met in middle school and have relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- Ethan noticed Gary was working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned and invited Gary to a weekend relaxation/rejuvenation retreat.
- Ethan told Gary that his health was as important as his dedication, that he hated seeing Gary like this, and asked him to go for just two days for a new perspective. Gary thanked him but refused, saying there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more behind Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- After the confrontation, Ethan heard Gary open up about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges Gary was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan offered to help Gary prioritize tasks and delegate some responsibilities, telling him he didn’t have to do everything himself. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and remaining challenges. Gary told him things were better, that Ethan’s help meant he was not as overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie the previous weekend. Ethan felt hopeful and proud and continued encouraging him.
- After a year, Ethan saw that Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him and decided to step back.
- Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away if needed, that he knew Gary had this, and to keep up the great work. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.

Ethan does not have access to Gary’s unspoken private thoughts, hidden hospital events, or any details Gary did not tell him.
